title: Who Was Exchanged in 1923?
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Mediterranean Travels
description: Apply five simplified rules of the 1923 Greek–Turkish population exchange convention to ten illustrative households and decide whether each was sent to Greece, sent to Turkey, or not exchanged.

educational.topic: Greco-Turkish War and the 1923 population exchange
learningObjectives: Apply the rules of the 1923 population exchange convention to ten household cases, deciding whether each was sent to Greece, sent to Turkey, or not exchanged, with at least 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt.
prerequisites: Convention Concerning the Exchange of Greek and Turkish Populations
Exemptions for Istanbul, Western Thrace, and Imbros and Tenedos
Rhodes as an Italian possession in 1923

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Rule application to worked cases with immediate feedback naming the deciding rule
keyQuestions: What did the convention use to decide who was exchanged: language, ethnicity, or religion?
Which groups were exempt, and why did half the cases stay?
Why was Rhodes untouched by the exchange?
commonMisconceptions: The exchange was decided by language or ethnicity.
Every Greek in Turkey was exchanged, including in Istanbul.
The exchange applied to every minority, including Jews.
The exchange applied to all the Greek islands, including Rhodes.
Refugees who had already fled in 1922 could go home once the war ended.
assessmentOpportunities: First-attempt score on ten cases (mastery: 8 of 10, with cases 3 and 4 correct).
Explain why a Turkish-speaking Orthodox family and a Greek-speaking Muslim family crossed the Aegean in opposite directions.
